facts.text: A Collision Mitigation System (CMS) detects an object close to a machine, warns the operator, and automatically applies the brakes if the operator does not react, to avoid a collision or reduce its severity.
facts.quote: A Collision Mitigation System (CMS) detects an object close to a machine, warns the operator, and if the operator does not react, applies the brakes automatically to avoid the collision or make it less severe.

facts.text: Collision mitigation means reducing harm rather than necessarily preventing a collision: late braking may still result in contact, but at lower speed.
facts.quote: To mitigate is to reduce the harm, not necessarily to prevent it: a system that brakes late may still make contact, but at lower speed.

facts.text: Volvo CE and Caterpillar both use the name Collision Mitigation System for their wheel-loader functions.
facts.quote: Volvo CE and Caterpillar both use the name for their wheel-loader functions [Chapter 2].

facts.text: The CMS to be validated by the program is the manufacturer's next-generation system.
facts.quote: In this booklet, "the CMS" means the manufacturer's next-generation system that is the subject of the whole program.

facts.text: The manufacturer already sells a proximity awareness system that warns the operator when the machine gets too close to an object.
facts.quote: The manufacturer already sells a proximity awareness system that warns the operator when the machine gets too close to an object

facts.text: Achieving an acceptable balance between hazard detection and false alarms in the manufacturer's existing proximity awareness system took years of calibration, with separate tuning required for each platform.
facts.quote: Getting it to an acceptable balance between detecting hazards and crying wolf took years of calibration, and each platform needed its own tuning [Introduction].

facts.text: The manufacturer's next-generation CMS retains the existing warnings and adds automatic braking.
facts.quote: The CMS keeps the warnings and adds the automatic brake.

facts.text: CMS prototype hardware and software are expected in mid-2027, after which validation must finish in under four months.
facts.quote: Prototype hardware and software are expected in mid-2027, and validation must then finish in under four months

facts.text: The last function comparable to the manufacturer's CMS took three to four years to validate.
facts.quote: validation must then finish in under four months, where the last comparable function took three to four years [Introduction].

facts.text: CMS validation must cover the complete chain: environment, sensor, object-recognition software, threat logic, warning and operator opportunity to act, intervention decision, machine-control interface, brake or retarder, actual machine motion, and resulting distance or collision.
facts.quote: Technically the CMS is a chain, and validation must cover all of it:

facts.text: The governing standard ISO 21815 limits CMS intervention to reducing speed, stopping, or preventing motion from standstill; automatic steering is excluded.
facts.quote: The governing standard, ISO 21815, limits intervention to reducing speed, stopping or preventing motion from standstill, never automatic steering [Chapters 1, 8].

facts.text: CMS is not a replacement for site design, traffic rules, or operator skill; in the industry's nine-level model, CMS occupies the top intervention level and works only with a sound baseline of lower-level controls.
facts.quote: It is not a replacement for site design, traffic rules or operator skill: in the industry's nine-level model it is the top level, intervention, which works only on a sound baseline of the lower levels [Chapters 1, 4].

facts.text: The research found no case in any industry of a new automatic braking function progressing from first representative hardware to accepted validation in about four months.
facts.quote: the research found no case in any industry of a new automatic braking function going from first representative hardware to accepted validation in about that time [Introduction, Chapters 1, 2, 13].

facts.text: The booklet concludes that the CMS program's four-month validation window cannot be compressed, but most validation work can be moved before prototype arrival.
facts.quote: The booklet's central conclusion is that the four months cannot be compressed but most of the work can be moved in front of them

facts.text: Before the CMS prototype arrives, the program should build the scenario catalog, the existing-fleet data pipeline, simulation and bench tools, and credibility evidence, making the subsequent four months a confirmation and calibration campaign.
facts.quote: build the scenario catalog, the data pipeline on the existing fleet, the simulation and bench tools and the credibility evidence before the prototype arrives, so the four months become a confirmation and calibration campaign [Introduction, Chapters 1, 10, 13].
